newsitem.title: UK: ED&F Man cuts '96/97 cocoa deficit to 125-150,000T.
newsitem.headline: ED&F Man cuts '96/97 cocoa deficit to 125-150,000T.

text.p: ED&F Man cut its 1996/97 cocoa deficit estimate to between 125,000 and 150,000 tonnes from its previous estimate in January of between 170,000 and 230,000 tonnes.
"Our estimate for this season's deficit has been reduced since our last report," it said in a report released on Thursday. "We are now expecting a deficit of 125-150,000 tonnes."
It said, "This would reduce world stocks to 1,085,000 tonnes at the end of the season, and the ratio of stocks to consumption is likely to fall to 39 percent."

The firm noted that the deficit had developed despite favourable weather in major producing countries. Unless the weather improved in West Africa, the market faced a substantial drawdown in 1997/98 stocks.

Regarding production, ED&F Man said it expected 1996/97 world cocoa bean production to fall seven percent to 2,688,000 tonnes from its current estimate of last year's crop of 2,882,000 tonnes. West African arrivals have been lower this year, with Ivory Coast currently down 70,000 tonnes from last year and Ghana purchases down 50,000 tonnes.

On consumption, it estimated 1995/96 world grindings up 6.2 percent to 2,694,000 tonnes, reflecting strong consumption growth in all markets. In 1996/97, it expected grindings to rise three to four percent to 2,795,000 tonnes, with most of the extra grind seen at origin, particularly West Africa.
